title: Interaction of Forces: Elastic Spring, Magnetic and Frictional Forces
subject: Science

questions.question: Two springs, Spring A and Spring B, are hung with identical 200g masses. Spring A extends 3cm. Spring B extends 7cm. Which spring is stiffer?
options: Spring A because it extended less under the same force
Spring B because it extended more under the same force
Both springs are equally stiff
Cannot be determined from the data
questions.answer: Spring A because it extended less under the same force
questions.explanation: A stiffer spring is harder to stretch. When the same force (200g mass) is applied, Spring A extended only 3cm while Spring B extended 7cm. The spring that extends less under the same force is stiffer.

questions.question: A student tests three springs by hanging different masses and measuring extension. For a 100g mass: Spring X extends 2cm, Spring Y extends 5cm, Spring Z extends 4cm. Which spring is the least stiff?
options: Spring X
Spring Y
Spring Z
All springs are equally stiff
questions.answer: Spring Y
questions.explanation: The least stiff spring extends the most under the same force. With a 100g mass, Spring Y extended 5cm, which is more than Spring X (2cm) and Spring Z (4cm). Therefore, Spring Y is the least stiff.

questions.question: Two identical springs are stretched by different forces. Spring P is pulled with 5N and extends 4cm. Spring Q is pulled with 10N and extends 4cm. Which spring is stiffer?
options: Spring P because it needed less force to extend the same amount
Spring Q because it needed more force to extend the same amount
Both springs are equally stiff
Cannot be determined from the data
questions.answer: Spring Q because it needed more force to extend the same amount
questions.explanation: A stiffer spring requires more force to stretch the same distance. Both springs extended 4cm, but Spring Q needed 10N while Spring P needed only 5N. Spring Q is stiffer because it required more force for the same extension.

questions.question: A spring is stretched by 6cm when a 300g mass is hung on it. If a 600g mass is hung on the same spring, what is the most likely extension?
options: 3cm
6cm
9cm
12cm
questions.answer: 12cm
questions.explanation: If the spring behaves consistently, doubling the force (from 300g to 600g) should double the extension. Since 300g caused 6cm extension, 600g would likely cause 12cm extension, assuming the spring is not stretched beyond its elastic limit.

questions.question: Two bar magnets are placed with their North poles facing each other. What will happen?
options: The magnets will attract each other
The magnets will repel each other
The magnets will not affect each other
The magnets will rotate to align side by side
questions.answer: The magnets will repel each other
questions.explanation: Like poles of magnets repel each other. When two North poles face each other, the magnetic force pushes them apart. This is called magnetic repulsion.

questions.question: A magnet attracts a steel paperclip from a distance of 8cm. If the magnet is moved to 15cm away from the paperclip, what will happen to the magnetic force?
options: The magnetic force will increase
The magnetic force will decrease
The magnetic force will stay the same
The magnetic force will become zero immediately
questions.answer: The magnetic force will decrease
questions.explanation: Magnetic force is a non-contact force that acts at a distance. The strength of the magnetic force decreases as the distance between the magnet and the magnetic object increases. At 15cm, the force will be weaker than at 8cm.

questions.question: A student places a magnet near a steel ball. The ball moves towards the magnet. Which statement best explains this observation?
options: The magnet pushes the ball with a contact force
The magnet pulls the ball with a magnetic force that acts at a distance
The ball is attracted to the magnet because of gravitational force
The ball moves because of frictional force
questions.answer: The magnet pulls the ball with a magnetic force that acts at a distance
questions.explanation: Magnetic force is a non-contact force. The magnet can pull the steel ball without touching it because magnetic force acts at a distance. Steel is a magnetic material, so it is attracted to the magnet.

questions.question: Two ring magnets are placed on a pencil. Magnet A has its North pole facing up. Magnet B is placed above Magnet A with its South pole facing down. What will happen?
options: The magnets will repel and move apart
The magnets will attract and stick together
The magnets will not affect each other
The magnets will rotate but not move
questions.answer: The magnets will attract and stick together
questions.explanation: Unlike poles attract. Magnet A has North pole up, Magnet B has South pole down. These are unlike poles facing each other, so they will attract and stick together.

questions.question: A student tests how distance affects magnetic force. She places a magnet at different distances from a paperclip and counts how many paperclips can be lifted. At 2cm: 5 paperclips. At 5cm: 2 paperclips. At 10cm: 0 paperclips. What can be concluded?
options: Magnetic force increases as distance increases
Magnetic force decreases as distance increases
Magnetic force does not depend on distance
Magnetic force is strongest at 10cm
questions.answer: Magnetic force decreases as distance increases
questions.explanation: The data shows that as distance increases from 2cm to 10cm, the number of paperclips lifted decreases from 5 to 0. This shows that magnetic force becomes weaker as the distance between the magnet and the object increases.

questions.question: A box is pushed across a rough floor. The student then adds oil to the floor and pushes the box again with the same force. What will happen to the distance the box travels?
options: The box will travel a shorter distance because oil increases friction
The box will travel a longer distance because oil reduces friction
The box will travel the same distance because oil does not affect friction
The box will not move at all because oil makes the floor slippery
questions.answer: The box will travel a longer distance because oil reduces friction
questions.explanation: Oil is a lubricant. Lubricants reduce frictional force between surfaces. With less friction opposing the motion, the box will travel a longer distance when pushed with the same force.

questions.question: Two springs are tested. Spring M extends 8cm with a 400g mass. Spring N extends 4cm with a 400g mass. Which statement is correct?
options: Spring M is stiffer than Spring N
Spring N is stiffer than Spring M
Both springs have the same stiffness
Spring M does not follow elastic spring force
questions.answer: Spring N is stiffer than Spring M
questions.explanation: With the same force (400g mass), Spring N extended only 4cm while Spring M extended 8cm. The spring that extends less under the same force is stiffer. Therefore, Spring N is stiffer than Spring M.

questions.question: A student hangs a spring from a stand and adds masses one by one. The extensions recorded are: 100g = 2cm, 200g = 4cm, 300g = 6cm. What extension is expected for a 500g mass?
options: 5cm
8cm
10cm
12cm
questions.answer: 10cm
questions.explanation: The data shows a pattern: every 100g increase causes 2cm more extension. For 500g, the extension would be 5 x 2cm = 10cm, assuming the spring is not stretched beyond its elastic limit.

questions.question: Why does adding grease to the moving parts of a bicycle make it easier to pedal?
options: Grease increases the gravitational force on the bicycle
Grease reduces the frictional force between moving parts
Grease makes the bicycle lighter
Grease increases the elastic spring force in the pedals
questions.answer: Grease reduces the frictional force between moving parts
questions.explanation: Grease is a lubricant. Lubricants reduce frictional force between surfaces that rub against each other. With less friction in the moving parts, less force is needed to pedal, making it easier to ride.

questions.question: A magnet is placed near four objects: iron nail, copper wire, plastic ruler, aluminium foil. Which object will be attracted to the magnet?
options: Copper wire
Plastic ruler
Aluminium foil
Iron nail
questions.answer: Iron nail
questions.explanation: Magnets attract magnetic materials. Iron is a magnetic material, so the iron nail will be attracted to the magnet. Copper, plastic, and aluminium are not magnetic materials and will not be attracted.

questions.question: Two identical springs are hung with different masses. Spring X has a 150g mass and extends 5cm. Spring Y has a 300g mass. What is the most likely extension of Spring Y?
options: 2.5cm
5cm
7.5cm
10cm
questions.answer: 10cm
questions.explanation: Spring Y has twice the mass (300g vs 150g) of Spring X. If the spring behaves consistently, twice the force should cause twice the extension. Since 150g caused 5cm extension, 300g would likely cause 10cm extension.

questions.question: A student places two magnets on a table. When she brings them closer, they suddenly push apart. What can she conclude about the poles facing each other?
options: The poles facing each other are unlike poles
The poles facing each other are like poles
One magnet is stronger than the other
The magnets are not magnetic
questions.answer: The poles facing each other are like poles
questions.explanation: Like poles of magnets repel each other. When the magnets suddenly push apart as they are brought closer, it means the poles facing each other are the same (both North or both South), causing magnetic repulsion.

questions.question: A toy car rolls down a ramp onto three different surfaces: Surface A (sandpaper), Surface B (wood), Surface C (oiled glass). On which surface will the car travel the farthest?
options: Surface A because sandpaper provides more grip
Surface B because wood is smooth
Surface C because oil reduces friction
All surfaces will give the same distance
questions.answer: Surface C because oil reduces friction
questions.explanation: Frictional force opposes motion. Sandpaper is rough and creates more friction. Oiled glass has a lubricant that reduces friction. With less friction on Surface C, the car will travel farther before stopping.

questions.question: A spring is compressed by pushing down on it. When released, the spring pushes back up. Why does this happen?
options: Gravitational force pulls the spring up
Elastic spring force acts to restore the spring to its original length
Magnetic force repels the spring upwards
Frictional force pushes the spring upwards
questions.answer: Elastic spring force acts to restore the spring to its original length
questions.explanation: When a spring is compressed, it stores elastic potential energy. The elastic spring force acts in the opposite direction to the compression, trying to return the spring to its original shape. This restoring force pushes the spring back up when released.

questions.question: A student tests two magnets. Magnet P attracts a paperclip from 12cm away. Magnet Q attracts a paperclip from 6cm away. Which magnet is stronger?
options: Magnet P because it can attract from a farther distance
Magnet Q because it attracts from a closer distance
Both magnets are equally strong
Cannot be determined from the data
questions.answer: Magnet P because it can attract from a farther distance
questions.explanation: A stronger magnet can exert magnetic force over a larger distance. Magnet P attracted the paperclip from 12cm away, while Magnet Q only attracted from 6cm. Since Magnet P worked from farther away, it is the stronger magnet.

questions.question: A spring balance is used to measure the weight of objects. When a heavier object is hung on it, the spring extends more. What property of the spring allows the spring balance to work?
options: The spring changes colour when stretched
The extension of the spring increases with more force applied
The spring becomes magnetic when stretched
The spring gets shorter when more force is applied
questions.answer: The extension of the spring increases with more force applied
questions.explanation: A spring balance works because the extension of the spring is related to the force applied. When a heavier object (more weight/force) is hung on it, the spring extends more. This relationship allows the scale to measure weight based on how far the spring stretches.
